Thanks Kim — quick executive view from me:

- We need the one-line impact statements by Wednesday to make the QBR narrative crisp (customer impact, revenue exposure, and go/no-go trigger).
- Two launches look amber: BrightGrid integration and the Large-Context performance rollout. If both slip, we need a prioritized scope reduction list that preserves the top-of-funnel velocity.
- Please put the final executive snapshot in the Drive folder (QBR-2028-LaunchPack) with a cover note.

I'm available for a 20-min pre-read review Thursday 08:30 PT.

-Vivek

Date: 2028-04-02T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR prep: roadmap snapshot, launch timelines & contingency lanes

Kim / all —

Summary from Prod Eng perspective (high level):

1) BrightGrid integration (owner: Monica) — high business priority, but dependency on BrightGrid's SSO cert rotation has introduced uncertainty. Current schedule assumes cert exchange by 4/10; if delayed beyond 4/12 we should scope to ship without SSO and enable it in a post-launch patch.

2) Large-Context perf rollout (owner: Karthik) — infra work is ~70% done; CPU-backed fallback has non-trivial perf delta. If we can't get GPU infra in time we should ship with a conservative token limit + throughput warning and a fast toggle for early customers.

I've attached a short playbook with proposed mitigations and tactical owners (contingency-playbook.pdf).

Open questions I need answers to:
- Do we have authority to defer SSO for BrightGrid for 2 weeks (Procurement + Legal ok with partial prod access)?
- Karthik: estimate on turning the fallback toggle into a feature flag we can flip per-customer.

Thanks — Monica

--
Monica Patel
Director, Customer Success Ops, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
Attachments: contingency-playbook.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-02T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR prep: roadmap snapshot, launch timelines & contingency lanes

Monica —

Short answers:
- We can make the customer-level fallback toggle work; estimate 2 dev days plus 1 day of QA to get a safe feature-flag gating in place. I'll push a small PR by EOD tomorrow and link the canary plan.
- If GPU infra isn't ready, the conservative token limit approach is low-risk and we can instrument the error/latency monitoring to auto-scale for affected customers.

I've dropped an initial canary plan into the Drive and attached a plaintext plan here (canary-rollout-plan.md).
